extractions.title: Immature excitatory neurons in the amygdala come of age during puberty.
extractions.quote: The PL contains a large population of immature excitatory neurons at birth, some of which may continue to be born from local progenitors. These progenitors disappear rapidly in infancy, but the immature neurons persist throughout childhood and adolescent ages, indicating that they develop on a protracted timeline.
